en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Sayabat and Abu Al Abbas, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When you do not know whether you have prayed three (Rak’at) or four, and your view falls upon the third, so build upon the third, and if your view falls upon the fourth, so offer Salām and complete. And if your imagination was equal, so complete and pray two Rak’at while you are seated’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from af-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Aban from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayabah and abu al-‘Abbas who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abdullah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If you do not know whether you have performed three or four Rak’ah and your thought settles on three, then consider it three. If your thought settles on four, say Salam (the phrase of offering greeting of peace) and end Salah (prayer). If your guess is equal; end Salah (prayer), then perform two Rak’ah in a sitting position.’”
